title: SmPC, leaflet and carton headings
text: The SmPC and the patient information leaflet use the standard headings, in order, as in the EU (QRD) templates that MHRA continues to accept; the carton gives the particulars of Schedule 24 in the usual order.
simplified: The app checks the headings of the UK documents in this pack; MHRA accepts the QRD-style headings for national products.

title: Required content is filled
text: Each required heading of the SmPC and the leaflet, and each mandatory particular of the carton, has content.

title: Black triangle
text: A medicine subject to additional monitoring in the UK shows the inverted black triangle and the standard statement before section 1 of the SmPC and after the name in the leaflet; others do not.

title: Yellow Card reporting
text: SmPC section 4.8 and the end of leaflet section 4 tell healthcare professionals and patients to report suspected adverse reactions through the Yellow Card Scheme (www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard or the MHRA Yellow Card app), not "the national reporting system listed in Appendix V".
simplified: The app checks for the Yellow Card Scheme and its web address, not every word of the paragraph.

title: UK marketing authorisation number
text: SmPC section 8 and the carton give the PL number (PL followed by five digits, a slash and four digits). An EU number (EU/1/...) does not belong on UK product information.
simplified: Numbers with the prefix PLGB or PLNI, from before 2025, raise a warning to check the number MHRA now holds for the UK-wide licence.

title: No EU-only references
text: UK texts do not refer to the European Medicines Agency, to Appendix V or to the EU annexes, and do not carry EU numbers or EU local representatives.

title: Holder established in the UK
text: The marketing authorisation holder named in SmPC section 7, the leaflet and the carton is established in the UK.
simplified: The app looks for "United Kingdom", "UK" or a UK postcode in the address.

title: "UK Only" on the pack
text: Every pack placed on the UK market from 1 January 2025 shows the words "UK Only" conspicuously on the outer packaging, legible, indelible and not hidden by other text, in a font of at least 7 point. Stickers were allowed only until 30 June 2025.
simplified: Traditional herbal and homeopathic registrations, and packs made only for export, are exempt; the app assumes a licensed medicine for the UK.

title: No EU safety features
text: The EU Falsified Medicines Directive safety features no longer apply anywhere in the UK. A 2D barcode and serial number are optional, but must not be recognisable by the European repository system. Anti-tamper devices are encouraged, not required.

title: Legal category
text: The carton gives the legal category: POM (prescription only medicine), P (pharmacy) or GSL (general sale list).
